subtitle: When the River Learned a New Tongue

panels.shot: sweeping wide of the Jhelum bank at dusk with Khanqah-e-Moula rising behind a contemplative figure
panels.action: Sayyid Ali Hamadani stands in calm profile on the riverbank, robes stirred by the evening wind, as wooden houses and the future site of Khanqah-e-Moula loom over the dark, slow Jhelum.

dialogue.text: In the troubled valley of fourteenth‑century Kashmir, Sayyid Ali Hamadani came with Sufi disciples and artisan networks—changing who prayed, who worked, and who mattered beside the Jhelum.

i18n.hi: चौदहवीं सदी के अशांत कश्मीर में सैय्यद अली हमदानी सूफी शागिर्दों और कारीगरों के साथ आए—झेलम किनारे यह बदला कि कौन इबादत करेगा, कौन काम करेगा, कौन अहम होगा।

panels.shot: high aerial over the Kashmir valley with Srinagar nestled along the Jhelum under soft snow peaks
panels.action: The Kashmir valley lies cradled between snow‑tipped mountains, the Jhelum cutting a silver path through clustered wooden dwellings of Srinagar under a pale sky.

dialogue.text: Kashmir in the late 1300s was a shaken land—Hindu dynasties fading, Turkic sultans rising, and the Brahmin chroniclers watching nervously as new powers entered the valley.

i18n.hi: 1300 के दशक के अंत का कश्मीर हिला हुआ था—हिंदू राजवंश ढल रहे थे, तुर्की सुल्तान उभर रहे थे, और ब्राह्मण इतिहासकार घबराए हुए नई ताकतों को घाटी में उतरते देख रहे थे।

panels.shot: medium wide of an early Sultanate court in Srinagar with throne, courtiers and a few turbaned foreign advisers
panels.action: Inside a timber‑pillared hall, Qutbu’d‑Din’s court gathers in layered Kashmiri robes; foreign‑looking scholars and administrators in turbans stand among local nobles, while scribes sit cross‑legged with palm‑leaf manuscripts.

dialogue.text: Under Sultan Qutbu’d‑Din, Persianate advisors and Sufi lineages were drawn into court, weaving the valley’s old Sanskrit world with the new networks of Central Asia and Iran.

i18n.hi: सुल्तान कुतुबुद्दीन के दरबार में फ़ारसी अलीम और सूफी सिलसिले बुलाए गए, जो पुरानी संस्कृत दुनिया को मध्य एशिया और ईरान के नए रिश्तों से बुन रहे थे।

panels.shot: close-up on Sayyid Ali Hamadani’s calm, weathered face against a backdrop of mountains and caravan silhouettes
panels.action: Sayyid Ali Hamadani is shown in dignified three‑quarter view, beard neatly trimmed, eyes thoughtful, a woolen shawl framing his face as distant caravan outlines move along a mountain pass behind him.

dialogue.text: From Hamadan, the Kubrawiya master Sayyid Ali Hamadani travelled widely—through Iran, Central Asia, and finally north to Kashmir—carrying scripture, craft knowledge, and the Sufi discipline of inner reform.

i18n.hi: हमदान से कुबrawिया पीर सैय्यद अली हमदानी दूर‑दूर घूमे—ईरान, मध्य एशिया, और आखिर उत्तर की तरफ़ कश्मीर—किताबें, हुनर और अंदरूनी सुधार का सूफी ज़िक्र साथ ले कर।

panels.shot: long shot of a caravan descending into the Kashmir valley, led by Hamadani on horseback
panels.action: A long file of pack animals and disciples winds down a forested slope; Sayyid Ali Hamadani rides at the front, staff resting across his saddle, as mist lifts to reveal the green bowl of the valley.

dialogue.text: Chronicles and Sufi traditions remember his arrival around 1379, under Qutbu’d‑Din’s reign, as caravans of disciples and artisans followed him into the cool, river‑cut valley.

i18n.hi: तारीख़ें और सूफी रिवायतें बताती हैं कि वे करीब 1379 में, कुतुबुद्दीन के दौर में आए, जब शागिर्दों और कारीगरों के क़ाफ़िले उनके पीछे ठंडी, नदी‑कटी घाटी में उतरे।

panels.shot: medium shot on Hamadani stepping onto the wooden ghats of the Jhelum with boats and old houses around
panels.action: Sayyid Ali Hamadani steps down to a wooden ghat, hand touching a carved railing, riverboats tied nearby, and tall timber houses leaning over the Jhelum’s slow current.

dialogue.text: He chose the river city—Srinagar on the Jhelum—as his base, a place where trade, rumor, and learning already flowed between the valley, the plains, and the lands far beyond.

i18n.hi: उन्होंने नदी किनारे का शहर चुना—झेलम पर श्रीनगर—अपना ठिकाना, जहाँ से पहले ही घाटी, मैदानी इलाकों और दूर देशों में कारोबार, ख़बर और इल्म बहता था।

panels.shot: interior wide of an early khanqah space near the river, crowded with people of varied dress and status
panels.action: Within a modest wooden hall by the water, Sayyid Ali Hamadani sits on a simple rug, disciples beside him, as boatmen, craftsmen, and a few robed scholars listen in mixed rows on the floor.

dialogue.text: Around him grew a khanqah—a Sufi lodge—where men of different backgrounds sat side by side, heard Qur’anic recitation, and shared meals outside the rigid hierarchies of caste.

i18n.hi: उनके इरद‑गिर्द एक ख़ानकाह उगी—सूफी आसरा—जहाँ अलग‑अलग पृष्ठभूमि के लोग साथ बैठते, क़ुरान की तिलावत सुनते, और जाति की सख़्त दीवारों से बाहर मिल‑जुल कर खाना खाते।

panels.shot: medium close on Hamadani teaching, hand raised, with attentive craftsmen and a Brahmin on the edge
panels.action: Sayyid Ali Hamadani sits upright, palm gently raised in explanation, while a weaver, a carpenter, and a boatman lean forward; a single Brahmin in sacred thread sits at the edge, brows furrowed.

dialogue.text: Before God, no lineage lifts one man above another. Only deeds do.

i18n.hi: ख़ुदा के आगे किसी ख़ानदान से कोई ऊँचा नहीं होता। ऊँचा करती हैं सिर्फ़ कर्म।

panels.shot: dim temple interior with a Brahmin writing on a manuscript, glancing uneasily toward the city
panels.action: Deep inside a stone‑based shrine, a Brahmin chronicler bends over a palm‑leaf manuscript, stylus poised, his face tight with concern as faint city sounds filter through the doorway.

dialogue.text: Jonaraja’s Dvitiya Rajatarangini hints at Brahmin unease: a teacher who spoke against caste welcomed those the old order kept at a distance, yet their conversions scarcely appear in his Sanskrit lines.

i18n.hi: जोनराज की द्वितीय राजतरंगिणी ब्राह्मण बेचैनी दिखाती है: एक उस गुरु की, जो जाति के ख़िलाफ़ बोलता, दूर रखे गए लोगों को बुलाता है, पर उनके इस्लाम कबूलने की आहट उसकी संस्कृत पंक्तियों में मुश्किल से झलकती है।

panels.shot: wide of an artisan courtyard where disciples and local craftsmen work with looms, metal and paper
panels.action: In a bustling courtyard, disciples of Hamadani guide local artisans at looms and small metal‑working stations; threads, tools and sheets of paper lie neatly arranged in the bright afternoon.

dialogue.text: Hamadani’s following included skilled men—textile workers, metal artisans, scribes—linking Kashmiri workshops more tightly to Persianate styles and markets, without originating every craft in the valley.

i18n.hi: हमदानी के साथ हुनरमंद लोग भी थे—कपड़ा मज़दूर, लोहे‑पीतल के कारीगर, लिपिक—जो कश्मीरी कारखानों को फ़ारसी अंदाज़ और बाज़ारों से मज़बूत जोड़ रहे थे, बिना कि हर हुनर घाटी में उन्हीं से शुरू हुआ हो।

panels.shot: medium shot inside the khanqah with Hamadani dictating and a disciple writing on paper
panels.action: Seated near a window, Sayyid Ali Hamadani recites measured verses as a young disciple dips his pen and copies onto fine paper, stacked beside older wooden manuscripts.

dialogue.text: He wrote and dictated works on ethics, devotion, and governance—texts that future sultans and scholars would cite, stitching Kashmiri religious practice into wider Persian and Central Asian debates.

i18n.hi: उन्होंने अख़लाक, इबादत और सल्तनत पर किताबें लिखीं और लिखवाईं—ऐसे मतन जिन्हें आगे चलकर सुल्तान और आलिम पढ़ेंगे, और कश्मीरी रिवायत को फ़ारसी और मध्य एशियाई बहसों से जोड़ेंगे।

panels.shot: courtly scene with Qutbu’d-Din listening to Hamadani in a wooden hall, courtiers watching closely
panels.action: In a wooden‑pillared audience chamber, Sultan Qutbu’d‑Din sits on a low throne, head slightly bowed, as Sayyid Ali Hamadani speaks calmly before him; courtiers observe in attentive silence.

dialogue.text: Sufi traditions and the Chaduraha chronicle remember court patronage for Hamadani’s circle, as Qutbu’d‑Din sought religious legitimacy and the prestige of ties to a renowned Kubrawiya master.

i18n.hi: सूफी रिवायतें और चादुरह का इतिहास याद करते हैं कि दरबार से हमदानी के हलके को सरपरस्ती मिली, जब कुतुबुद्दीन को दीन की legitimi और मशहूर कुबrawिया पीर से रिश्ते का वज़न चाहिए था।

panels.shot: night-time exterior of the early khanqah, lamps glowing, with silhouettes of visitors entering
panels.action: Under a star‑strewn sky, oil lamps glow along the wooden façade of the riverside khanqah; silhouettes of diverse figures step through the doorway toward the murmur of prayer and discussion.

dialogue.text: For many lower‑status groups, the khanqah became a space where they could belong, pray, and learn together; their quiet movement toward Islam is largely invisible in Brahmin‑authored records.

i18n.hi: बहुत‑से नीची हैसियत वाले तबकों के लिए ख़ानकाह ऐसी जगह बनी जहाँ वे अपने लगें, साथ नमाज़ पढ़ें और सीखें; उनका धीरे‑धीरे इस्लाम की तरफ़ झुकना ब्राह्मण लिखे रिकॉर्ड में लगभग ग़ायब है।

panels.shot: medium shot of Hamadani preparing to depart, disciples around him, Jhelum in the background
panels.action: Sayyid Ali Hamadani stands near packed bundles and saddled animals, disciples gathered close, as the Jhelum gleams behind them and the khanqah’s wooden frame rises on the bank.

dialogue.text: Hamadani did not remain in Kashmir for life; his visits were episodes in a wider Sufi journey. Yet the networks he set in motion stayed after he rode out of the valley.

i18n.hi: हमदानी उम्र भर कश्मीर में नहीं रहे; उनके कश्मीरी दिन एक बड़े सूफी सफ़र की कड़ियाँ थे। पर जो रिश्ते उन्होंने चला दिए, वे उनके घाटी से निकल जाने के बाद भी टिके रहे।

panels.shot: time-lapse style wide showing the same riverside spot evolving into the Khanqah-e-Moula structure
panels.action: The riverside location is shown over implied years—first a modest lodge, then expanded wooden galleries and carved eaves—until a full Khanqah‑e‑Moula rises above the water in rich detail.

dialogue.text: In 1395, on the remembered site of his stay, the Khanqah‑e‑Moula was built, fixing his presence into wood and stone so that memory of the stranger from Hamadan outlived his physical visits.

i18n.hi: 1395 में, उनकी याद की गई ठहरने वाली जगह पर ख़ानकाह‑ए‑मौला बनी, जिसने उनकी मौजूदगी को लकड़ी और पत्थर में जड़ दिया, ताकि हमदान से आए इस अजनबी की याद उसके जाने के बाद भी ज़िंदा रहे।

panels.shot: interior of Khanqah-e-Moula with worshippers and artisans side by side, light streaming through lattice
panels.action: Inside the Khanqah‑e‑Moula, worshippers stand and bow in orderly lines, a few with ink‑stained hands and artisan tools tucked at their belts, as soft daylight filters through wooden lattice screens.

dialogue.text: Over time, Sufi lodges like this anchored a Persianate Muslim presence in Srinagar, mixing devotional life with artisan patronage and shaping how faith, work, and authority met along the river.

i18n.hi: धीरे‑धीरे ऐसी सूफी ख़ानकाहों ने श्रीनगर में फ़ारसी रंग की मुसलमान मौजूदगी को थाम लिया, इबादत को कारीगर सरपरस्ती से मिलाकर यह गढ़ा कि नदी किनारे कैसे धर्म, मेहनत और हुक्मरानी टकराते और मिलते हैं।

panels.shot: somber court scene of a later Sultan Sikandar with Sayyid Muhammad Hamadani advising beside him
panels.action: In a more formal court, Sultan Sikandar sits sternly robed while Sayyid Muhammad Hamadani, Hamadani’s son, stands respectfully at his side, advisors and guards lined in controlled symmetry.

dialogue.text: Later, his son Sayyid Muhammad Hamadani would counsel Sultan Sikandar, a reign remembered for stricter religious policies—a reminder that Sufi influence in Kashmir could both soften and harden boundaries.

i18n.hi: बाद में उनके बेटे सैय्यद मुहम्मद हमदानी ने सुल्तान सिकंदर को मशवरा दिया, जिसका दौर सख़्त धार्मिक नीतियों के लिए याद है—याद दिलाते हुए कि कश्मीर में सूफी असर कभी सीमाएँ नरम, तो कभी सख़्त कर सकता है।

panels.shot: present-day style wide of Khanqah-e-Moula with a faint superimposed image of Hamadani by the river
panels.action: The Khanqah‑e‑Moula stands in full present‑day detail on the Jhelum’s bank, worshippers moving below; faintly above the water, an almost transparent figure of Sayyid Ali Hamadani looks on, hands folded.

dialogue.text: Today, when the Jhelum touches the Khanqah‑e‑Moula, it still carries the layered memory of Hamadani’s visits—of words against caste, of new craft ties, and of how travelling people quietly remake a land.

i18n.hi: आज भी, जब झेलम ख़ानकाह‑ए‑मौला को छूती है, वह हमदानी के आने‑जाने की परतदार याद लेकर बहती है—जाति के ख़िलाफ़ बोल, नए हुनरों की डोरें, और उन मुसाफ़िरों की जो चुपचाप किसी ज़मीन को नया रूप दे जाते हैं।
